paper_id: ViTAD_ Timing Violation-Aware Debugging of RTL Code using Large Language Models
title: ViTAD: Timing Violation-Aware Debugging of RTL Code using Large Language Models
motivation: Manual RTL timing debugging is error-prone, inefficient, and relies heavily on scarce expert experience in VLSI design
problem_framing: Timing violations cause functional failures; debugging requires pinpointing faulty paths, analyzing root causes, and modifying design without altering functionality
key_insight: Joint modeling of code structure and timing via Signal Timing Dependency Graph enables LLM to reason about violation causes with explicit causality
method_signature: STDG construction + violation path extraction + scenario-based knowledge retrieval + dynamic repair template generation
evaluation_criteria: Fix Rate (FR) = c/n across 54 timing violation cases from open-source RTL projects
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: LLM cannot accurately determine control signals for asynchronous transmission; complex/large code exceeds LLM processing capacity
evidence_for_taste: error-prone and inefficient due to limited engineer experience
cause descriptions greatly improve repair success
clear causality enables LLMs to infer repair strategies
incorporating iterative or backtracking mechanisms may improve
the provided prompts lack sufficient specificity
